instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires periodic expense statements to be filed by registered principals, with lobbyists only providing information to the principal for the principal’s filing, so lobbyists are not required to file their own periodic spending reports.
Semiannual filing is imposed on principals (“Every principal...shall, on or before July 31 and January 31, file...”), not on lobbyists as filers of a spending report.
The only periodic expense statements described are principal statements filed twice per year for 6‑month reporting periods, and there is no annual lobbyist spending report required.
The statute specifies filings on or before July 31 and January 31 (covering the preceding reporting period), and does not provide for quarterly lobbyist spending reports.
No monthly spending report is required; the only periodic expense statement filing deadlines stated are July 31 and January 31 for principals.
There is no triannual filing schedule in the statute; the only periodic reporting deadlines are twice yearly for principal expense statements.
The statute does not create any other cadence options for lobbyists to file spending reports because it does not require lobbyist-filed periodic spending reports.
Periodic expense statements are filed by principals (twice yearly), while lobbyists only supply information to principals, so there is no lobbyist spending report cadence.
Total lobbying expenditures are reported in the principal’s expense statement, not in any lobbyist-filed spending report required by statute.
Compensation to lobbyists is included in the principal’s aggregate lobbying expenditures, and the statute does not require lobbyists themselves to file a report stating total compensation.
Expense categorization requirements are imposed on principals in their expense statements, and there is no lobbyist spending report to categorize expenses.

The statute requires the principal to file expense statements and to file a copy of lobbyist-supplied information, but it does not require lobbyists to file an itemized spending report as the reporting party.
Lobbyists must provide information needed for the principal’s statement, but the law does not impose a lobbyist-filed itemized expenses report.
The payer-by-lobbyist breakdown (listing a lobbyist if payments exceed $200) appears in the principal’s expense statement, not as a lobbyist reporting requirement.
The only issue-related breakdown required is a principal’s estimate of time by proposal/topic, not expenditures per issue in a lobbyist spending report.

General issues/topics are reported by principals under the topic identification/reporting provisions, and the statute does not require lobbyists to disclose issues in a periodic spending report they file.
Subject matter/topic identification is a principal reporting obligation, and the statute does not create a lobbyist-filed spending report including subject matter.
Identifying legislative proposals, budget bill subjects, and proposed administrative rule numbers is required of principals, not of lobbyists in a periodic spending report.
Bill/proposal identification is reported by principals to the commission, and no lobbyist spending report requiring bill numbers is specified.
The statute requires principals to report proposals/topics but does not require any filer (and specifically not lobbyists) to report positions taken on bills in a spending report.
The daily itemization of time spent meeting with officials is part of the principal’s expense statement requirements, not a lobbyist spending report.
Lobbyist address information is part of the license application (a registration/licensing form), and the statute does not require a lobbyist periodic spending report containing lobbyist contact info.
Principal names are disclosed via principal registration and lobbyist authorization filings, but there is no lobbyist-filed periodic spending report requiring listing of principals represented.
Principal name and business address are required in the principal’s registration statement, not as part of a lobbyist-filed spending report.
Business activity/nature and purposes are required disclosures in the principal’s registration statement, not a lobbyist periodic spending report.
Indirect costs like office overhead are elements of the principal’s expense statement, and the statute does not require lobbyists to report indirect costs in their own periodic spending reports.

While gifts/transport/lodging to officials are generally prohibited, the only periodic expense reporting requirement is for principals and does not create a lobbyist spending report disclosing such items.
Because the statute does not require lobbyists to file periodic spending reports at all, it likewise does not require lobbyists to file a zero-activity spending report.

The principal’s expense statement reports reimbursements to specified officials/candidates, but the statute does not require lobbyist spending reports or extend such reporting to household members of officials.
